VII.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=7|verse=11}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 15 Sunday after Pentecost. And vpō Thursday in the 4 weeke of Lent. And for S. Monica S. Augustins mother Maij. 4.}}And it came to passe, aftervvard he vvent into a citie that is called Naim: and there vvent vvith him his Disciples and a very great multitude. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=12}}† And vvhen he came nigh to the gate of the citie, behold a dead man vvas caried forth, the only sonne of his mother: and she, vvas a vvidovv: and a great multitude of the citie vvith her. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=13}}† Vvhom vvhen our Lord had seen, being moued vvith mercie vpon her, he said to her, VVeepe not. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=14}}† And he came neere and touched the coffin. And they that caried it, stood stil: and he said, Yong man, I say to thee, Arise. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=15}}† And he that vvas dead, sate vp, and beganne to speake. And he gaue him to his mother. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=16}}† And feare tooke them al: and they magnified God, saying, That a great Prophet is risen among vs: and, That God hath visited his people. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=17}}† And this saying vvent forth into al Ievvrie of him, and into al the countrie about.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=18}}† And Iohns disciples shevved him of al these things. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=19}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 11, 2.''}}* And Iohn called tvvo of his disciples, and sent them to {{sc|Iesvs}}, saying, Art thou he that art to come: or expect vve an other? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=20}}† And vvhen the men vvere come vnto him, they said, Iohn the Baptist hath sent vs to thee, saying, Art thou he that art to come: or expect vve an other? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=21}}† (And the self same houre, he cured many of maladies, and hurtes, and euil spirits: and to many blinde he {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ἐχαρίσατο.}}∷ gaue sight.) {{verse|chapter=7|verse=22}}† And answering, he said to them, Goe and report to Iohn vvhat you haue heard and seen: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 35, 5. 61, 1.''}}* That the blinde see, the lame vvalke, the lepers are made cleane, the deafe heare, the dead rise againe, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=23}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Pauperes euangelizantur'', that is, to the poore the Gospel is preached, and they receiue it.}}∷ the poore are euangelized: and blessed is he vvhosoeuer shal not be scandalized in me.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=24}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 11, 7.''}}* And vvhen Iohns messengers vvere departed, he began to say of Iohn to the multitudes, VVhat vvent you out into the desert to see? a reede moued vvith the vvinde? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=25}}† But vvhat vvent you forth to see? a man clothed in {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Marke this vvel concerning Iohns apparel and diet. See the Annotations vpon S. Matth. ''c. 3, 4''.}}∷ soft garments? behold they that are in costly apparel and delicacies, are in the house of kings. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=26}}† But what vvent you out for to see? a Prophet? Certes I say to you, and more then a Prophet. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=27}}† this is he of vvhom it is vvritten, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mal. 3, 1.''}}* ''Behold I send mine Angel before thy face, vvhich shal prepare thy vvay before thee''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=28}}† For I say to you, A greater Prophet among the children of vvomen then Iohn the Baptist, there is no man. but he that is the lesser in the kingdom of God, is greater then he. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=29}}† And al the people hearing and the Publicans, iustified God, being baptized vvith<noinclude>{{rh|||Iohns}}</noinclude>
